stories.title: From a VR gay sauna to the gothic pile that inspired Cluedo – Fierce festival storms back
stories.summary: Birmingham's Fierce festival is returning with a live-art program that includes a VR gay sauna, late-night artist dinners, a swimming-pool performance and Faye Driscoll's rotating disintegration. The Guardian describes it as Britain's longest-running live-art festival and highlights work that can feel both confusingly self-indulgent and profound.

links.headline: From a VR gay sauna to the gothic pile that inspired Cluedo – Fierce festival storms back
links.excerpt: Venues across Birmingham As Britain’s longest-running live art festival returns, get ready for late-night artist dinners, a show in a swimming pool and Faye Driscoll’s incredible rotating disintegration The phrase “two things can be true” is a frequent refrain in popular psychology and it’s also a frequent response, I find, to witnessing the farther reaches of live art. Hmm, is this performance confusingly self-indulgent or utterly profound? Sometimes it can be both.

stories.title: Penguin Colony review – an Antarctic odyssey of Nazis and Lovecraftian horrors
stories.summary: Penguin Colony is an offbeat PC adventure from Origame Digital in which a small penguin crosses Antarctica in search of an eldritch entity. The game mixes Nazi imagery with Lovecraftian horror, creating an odd but absorbing world that becomes stranger as the journey unfolds.
